study_identification.title: Individualized gray matter morphological abnormalities unveil two neuroanatomical obsessive-compulsive disorder subtypes

preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The preprocessing pipeline is described in the paper.
preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: Voxel-wise gray matter volume (GMV) for each participant was derived using voxel-based morphometry in the CAT 12 toolbox (http:// dbm.neuro.uni-jena.de/cat12/). The standard CAT 12 pipeline was followed, as detailed in reference [35]. This pipeline encompassed bias-field correction, brain segmentation into gray and white matter and cerebrospinal fluid, correction for partial volume effects, normalization to Montreal Neurological Institute space, resampling to 1.5 mm³, and nonlinear modulation [35, 36]. Subsequently, the gray matter maps underwent smoothing with a 6-mm full width at half maximum Gaussian kernel.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Two-sample t-test, k-means clustering, multilinear model, dominance analysis
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Two distinct OCD subtypes were identified with opposite patterns of gray matter abnormalities.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Two OCD subtypes were identified based on individualized gray matter morphological abnormalities. Subtype 1 showed increased gray matter volume in several brain regions, while subtype 2 exhibited decreased gray matter volume in other regions. These subtypes had different disease epicenters and were associated with different neurotransmitter receptors/transporters.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The study was cross-sectional, had limited clinical information, and the patient sample had lower educational levels than controls.
